original_question: If the trivializing vector field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} for the tetrahedral flow in dimension d+1 can be constructed from sunflower descendants, determine whether it is enough to use the union of two classes of dimension-(d+1) descendants: first, descendants of the previously known dimension-d solution X_{gamma_3}^d, and second, descendants of vanishing one-vector micro-graphs defined over R^d.
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the second item in the paper’s final open-problems list: after asking whether the trivializing field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} can be obtained from linear combinations of 2D sunflower descendants, the paper asks whether one may in fact restrict to the union of two families of (d+1)-dimensional descendants, namely those coming from the known d-dimensional solution X_{gamma_3}^d and those coming from vanishing 1-vector Nambu micro-graphs over R^d. Proposition 1 is nearby evidence for this strategy in the special case d=3 to 4, but it is not itself the exact target statement.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right object X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}, the tetrahedral-flow trivialization problem, the conditional dependence on sunflower descendants, and the two descendant classes singled out by the paper: descendants of the lower-dimensional solution X_{gamma_3}^d and descendants of vanishing 1-vector micro-graphs over R^d.
missing_details: The ambient class must be specified: the question is about Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets on affine real space R^{d+1}, not arbitrary Poisson brackets.

The underlying bracket should be stated explicitly: {f,g}_{d+1}(x) = rho(x) det(partial(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-1}) / partial(x^1,...,x^{d+1})), with Casimirs a_i; the paper introduces this as Eq. (1) in dimension d and the open problem concerns the shift d to d+1.
The exact triviality hypothesis should be written: assuming the restricted tetrahedral flow is a Poisson coboundary, Q_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{tensor 4}) = [[P, X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{tensor 3})]].

The conditional phrase 'if yes' from the immediately preceding open problem is essential: the paper first asks whether X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} is obtainable from linear combinations of 2D sunflower descendants at all.
The paper speaks of linear combinations of descendants, not merely of being 'constructed from' them in an unspecified way.
The source sunflower should be identified exactly as the 2D graph X^{gamma_3} = (0,1;1,3;1,2) + 2·(0,2;1,3;1,2).

The term 'descendant' needs the paper’s specific meaning: in the shift d to d+1, one adjoins the new Casimir a_{d-1} to each Levi-Civita vertex and expands any external arrow hitting an old Casimir via the Leibniz rule.

The relevant micro-graphs here are 1-vector Nambu micro-graphs with m = 1 sink and n = 3 copies of the Nambu bracket, because these are the objects used to build a trivializing vector field for the tetrahedral flow.
The dimension range should be made explicit: this is posed in the paper’s open-problem regime for the shift d to d+1 with d+1 > 3, i.e. effectively starting from d >= 3 in this context.
The phrase 'vanishing 1-vector micro-graphs' should be clarified to mean vanishing as formulas, phi(Gamma) = 0, not merely graph-theoretically zero.

No homogeneity assumption, polynomial degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or 'for all sufficiently large m' quantifier appears in this paper’s formulation; a faithful rewrite should not introduce any of these.
refined_question: Let P be a Nambu-determinant Poisson bivector on the affine space R^{d+1}, given by {f,g}_{d+1}(x) = rho(x) det(partial(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-1}) / partial(x^1,...,x^{d+1})). Assume that the restricted tetrahedral flow in dimension d+1 is trivial on this Nambu class, so that Q_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{tensor 4}) = [[P, X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{tensor 3})]], and assume further that X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} is sought as a linear combination of (d+1)-dimensional descendants of the 2D sunflower graph X^{gamma_3} = (0,1;1,3;1,2) + 2·(0,2;1,3;1,2). Is it then sufficient to search for X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} only in the union of (i) the (d+1)-descendants of the underlying d-dimensional solution X_{gamma_3}^d and (ii) the (d+1)-descendants of vanishing 1-vector Nambu micro-graphs over R^d, where 'descendant' is understood in the paper’s d to d+1 sense of adjoining the new Casimir and expanding by the Leibniz rule?
justification: The wording of your draft matches the second bullet in the paper’s final open-problems list much more closely than Proposition 1 itself. The paper first sets up the Nambu-determinant bracket and the general triviality question for the tetrahedral cocycle action in Section 1. It then defines Nambu micro-graphs, descendants, and embeddings in Section 2, and explains that the trivializing 1-vectors are sought among micro-graphs with one sink and three Nambu blocks. Proposition 1 proves a special d=3 to 4 descendant-closure statement for vanishing descendants of the sunflower, namely that no extra vanishing 4D descendants need be sought outside descendants of the relevant 3D vanishing set. The final bullet list on page 95 then asks, in general, whether once one works inside 2D sunflower descendants, the search for X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} can be restricted to the union of descendants of X_{gamma_3}^d and descendants of vanishing 1-vector micro-graphs over R^d. That is exactly the paper-faithful sharpened version of your draft.
